title.zh: 卷一百六十一 列傳第八十六 張趙李鄭徐王馮庾
title.en: Volume 161 Biographies 86: Zhang, Zhao, Li, Zheng, Xu, Wang, Feng, Yu
title.raw: 卷一百六十一 列傳第八十六 張趙李鄭徐王馮庾 Volume 161 Biographies 86: Zhang, Zhao, Li, Zheng, Xu, Wang, Feng, Yu

sentences.zh: 張趙李鄭徐王馮庾

translations.literal: Zhang, Zhao, Li, Zheng, Xu, Wang, Feng, Yu
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, Zhao, Li, Zheng, Xu, Wang, Feng, and Yu

sentences.zh: 張薦，字孝舉，深州陸澤人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jian, style name Xiaoju, was a native of Luzhe in Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian, whose style was Xiaoju, came from Luzhe in Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖鷟，字文成，早惠絕倫。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Zhang Zhuo, style name Wencheng, who in youth was gifted beyond all peers.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhang Zhuo, styled Wencheng, had shown a precocious brilliance unmatched among his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 為兒時，夢紫文大鳥，五色成文，止其廷。

translations.literal: As a child he dreamed of a great bird with purple markings, its five colors forming patterns, which stopped in his courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: In childhood he dreamed of a great bird marked in purple, its five hues woven into patterned writing, alighting in his courtyard.

sentences.zh: 大父曰：「吾聞五色赤文，鳳也；

translations.literal: His grandfather said: "I have heard that five colors with red markings are the phoenix;
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather said, "I have heard that when the five colors show red markings, the bird is a phoenix;

sentences.zh: 紫文，鸑鷟也。

translations.literal: purple markings are the yuanchu."
translations.idiomatic: when they show purple markings, it is a yuanchu."

sentences.zh: 若壯，殆以文章瑞朝廷乎？

translations.literal: When you grow up, might you perhaps bring literary glory as an auspicious omen to the court?
translations.idiomatic: When you come of age, will you perhaps bring literary brilliance to the court as an auspicious sign?

sentences.zh: 」遂命以名。

translations.literal: " Accordingly he was given the name [Wencheng].
translations.idiomatic: " And so he was given the name Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 調露初，登進士第。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Diaolu era he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Diaolu reign he took the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 考功員外郎騫味道見所對，稱天下無雙。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zhang Qianchao of the Bureau of Evaluations saw his examination answers and declared him matchless under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qianchao, supervising secretary in the Bureau of Evaluations, read his examination papers and pronounced him without peer under heaven.

sentences.zh: 授岐王府參軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed aide in the household of the Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He was made an aide in the Prince of Qi's household.

sentences.zh: 八以制舉皆甲科，再調長安尉，遷鴻臚丞。

translations.literal: Eight times he took the irregular recruitment examination and each time received top grade; twice he was transferred as magistrate of Chang'an, then promoted to aide at the Court of Diplomatic Reception.
translations.idiomatic: Eight times he entered the special recruitment examinations and each time earned the highest grade; after two postings as magistrate of Chang'an he was promoted to aide at the Court of Diplomatic Reception.

sentences.zh: 四參選，判策為銓府最。

translations.literal: On four occasions he entered selection for office; his policy examination essays ranked highest in the Board of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the selection process four times, and his policy essays each time ranked first in the Board of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 員外郎員半千數為公卿稱「鷟文辭猶青銅錢，萬選萬中」，時號鷟「青錢學士」。

translations.literal: Vice Director Yuan Banqian repeatedly praised him before the chief ministers, saying "Zhuo's literary compositions are like bronze coins—every selection hits the mark," and at the time Zhuo was called "the Green-Coin Scholar."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Yuan Banqian often told the chief ministers that "Zhuo's prose is like bronze cash—pick any piece and it rings true," and people of the day nicknamed Zhuo "the Green-Coin Scholar."

sentences.zh: 證聖中，天官侍郎劉奇以鷟及司馬锽為御史。

translations.literal: During the Zhengsheng era, Vice Director of the Bureau of Personnel Liu Qi recommended Zhuo and Sima Zheng as censors.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengsheng period, Liu Qi, vice director of the Bureau of Personnel, nominated Zhuo and Sima Zheng for posts as censors.

sentences.zh: 性躁卞，儻蕩無檢，罕為正人所遇，姚崇尤惡之。

translations.literal: His nature was irascible and overbearing; he was unbridled and without restraint, rarely met with approval from upright men, and Yao Chong especially detested him.
translations.idiomatic: He was hot-tempered and overbearing, reckless and without propriety, seldom found favor with upright officials, and Yao Chong hated him above all.

sentences.zh: 開元初，御史李全交劾鷟多口語訕短時政，貶嶺南；

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kaiyuan era, Censor Li Quanjiao impeached Zhuo for frequent slanderous talk mocking current affairs, and he was demoted to Lingnan;
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan, Censor Li Quanjiao charged Zhuo with habitually mocking current affairs in speech, and he was banished to Lingnan;

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書李日知訟斥太重，得內徙。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Li Rizhi petitioned that the punishment was excessively harsh, and he was allowed an internal transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Li Rizhi protested that the sentence was too severe, and Zhuo was permitted to move to an interior post instead.

sentences.zh: 鷟屬文下筆輒成，浮艷少理致，其論著率詆誚蕪猥，然大行一時，晚進莫不傳記。

translations.literal: Zhuo composed essays that flowed from his brush at once; they were ornate but shallow in reasoning, and his treatises mostly ridiculed things as vulgar and trivial, yet they were widely circulated for a time and younger scholars all copied and circulated them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo's essays came from his brush fully formed; they were florid but thin in substance, and his writings mostly derided others as coarse and base, yet for a time they circulated everywhere and every rising scholar copied and passed them along.

sentences.zh: 武後時，中人馬仙童陷默啜，問：「文成在否？

translations.literal: During Empress Wu's reign, the eunuch Ma Xiantong was trapped by Mohe chieftain Mokch'o and was asked: "Is Wencheng still alive?"
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu, the eunuch Ma Xiantong fell into Mokch'o's hands and was asked, "Is Wencheng still at court?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「近自御史貶官。

translations.literal: " He answered: "He was recently demoted from his post as censor."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "He was recently demoted from his censor's post."

sentences.zh: 」曰：「國有此人不用，無能為也。

translations.literal: " [Mokch'o] said: "When a state has such a man and does not use him, it can accomplish nothing."
translations.idiomatic: " Mokch'o said, "A state that has such a man and will not employ him can achieve nothing."

sentences.zh: 」新羅、日本使至，必出金寶購其文。

translations.literal: When envoys from Silla and Japan arrived, they invariably brought out gold and treasures to purchase his writings.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever envoys from Silla or Japan came, they would offer gold and precious goods to buy his writings.

sentences.zh: 終司門員外郎。

translations.literal: He ended his career as vice director of the Gate Office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as vice director of the Gate Office.

sentences.zh: 薦敏銳有文辭，能為《周官》、《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: Jian was keen and possessed literary talent; he could compose on the Offices of Zhou and the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was quick-witted and skilled in letters; he could write on the Offices of Zhou and the Zuo Commentary.

sentences.zh: 初，為顏真卿嘆賞。

translations.literal: At first he was admired and praised by Yan Zhenqing.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Yan Zhenqing praised him highly.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，浙西觀察使李涵表薦才任史官，詔授左司禦率府兵曹參軍，以母老辭不就。

translations.literal: During the Dali era, Li Han, commissioner of the Zhexi circuit, memorialized that Jian's talent suited him for the office of historian; an edict appointed him military aide in the Left Bureau of the Imperial Guard Command, but he declined on account of his mother's age.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali period Li Han, commissioner of Zhexi, recommended Jian as fit for historiography; the court appointed him military aide in the Left Bureau of the Imperial Guard Command, but he declined because his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 喪除，禮部侍郎於邵以聞，召充史館修撰，兼陽翟尉。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, Vice Minister of Rites Yu Shao reported this, and he was summoned to serve as compiler in the Historiography Office, concurrently as magistrate of Yangzhai.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning period ended, Vice Minister of Rites Yu Shao reported the fact, and Jian was summoned to the Historiography Office as compiler, while also holding the post of magistrate of Yangzhai.

sentences.zh: 真卿為李希烈所拘，遣兄子峴及家仆奏事，五輩皆留內客省，不得出。

translations.literal: Zhenqing was detained by Li Xilie; he sent his elder brother's son Xian and household servants to present memorials, five parties in all, but all were detained in the Inner Reception Office and not permitted to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing was held captive by Li Xilie and sent his nephew Xian and household servants to report to court; all five parties were kept in the Inner Reception Office and denied release.

sentences.zh: 薦上疏曰：

translations.literal: Jian submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Jian submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 去正月中，真卿奉使淮西，期不先戒，行無素備。

translations.literal: Last first month, Zhenqing was sent on mission to the Huai west, with no advance warning of the deadline and no habitual preparations for the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Last month Zhenqing was dispatched on a mission to Huai west without prior notice of the deadline and without his usual preparations for travel.

sentences.zh: 受命之後，不宿於家，親黨不遑告別，介副不及陳請，孱僮單騎，即日載馳。

translations.literal: After receiving the commission he did not lodge at home; kin and friends had no time for farewells; aides and deputies had no chance to present requests; with a frail servant and a single mount he set out that very day at full speed.
translations.idiomatic: Once he received the commission he did not spend a night at home; relatives and friends had no chance to bid him farewell; aides and deputies could not even present their requests; with only a weak servant and a lone horse he set out that same day at full gallop.

sentences.zh: 冒奸鋒於臨汝，折元惡於許下，捐軀杖義，威詬群兇，遂令脅制者回慮，忠勇者肆情。

translations.literal: He braved the traitors' blades at Linyu and broke the chief villain at Xuchang; he gave his body to uphold righteousness and awed and rebuked the whole band of villains, so that those who had been coerced reconsidered and the loyal and brave gave full vent to their feelings.
translations.idiomatic: He faced the rebels' blades at Linyu and broke the ringleader at Xuchang; risking his life for righteousness, he awed and denounced the whole gang of traitors, so that those who had been coerced turned back in thought and the loyal and brave could act freely.

sentences.zh: 周曾奮發於外，韋清伺應於內，希烈蒼黃窘迫，奔固舊穴，蓋真卿義風所激也。

translations.literal: Zhou Zeng roused himself without; Wei Qing watched and responded within; Xilie, flustered and pressed, fled to secure his old lair—all this, surely, was stirred by Zhenqing's righteous spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zeng took action from without, Wei Qing coordinated from within; Xilie, panicked and cornered, ran back to hold his old stronghold—all stirred, no doubt, by the force of Zhenqing's righteousness.

sentences.zh: 真卿逮事四朝，為國元老，忠直孝友，羽儀王室。

translations.literal: Zhenqing has served through four reigns, is a senior statesman of the realm, loyal, upright, filial, and friendly, an ornament to the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqing has served four reigns and stands among the realm's elder statesmen—loyal, upright, filial, and devoted—a pillar of the royal house.

sentences.zh: 行年八十，被羸老之疾，拘囚環堵之間，顧眄鉤戟之下，呼嗟憤恚，失寢忘食，不知悲翁何以堪此！

translations.literal: He is eighty years old, afflicted with frailty and old age, imprisoned within four walls, looking up beneath hooked halberds; he sighs and rages, loses sleep and forgets food—who knows how this grieving old man can bear it!
translations.idiomatic: He is eighty, worn by age and illness, confined within four walls, living under the threat of halberds; he sighs in anger, cannot sleep or eat—how can such a grieving elder endure this!

sentences.zh: 伏聞希烈之母，鐘念幼子，目不絕泣，求責希烈；

translations.literal: I have heard that Xilie's mother, deeply mindful of her younger son, weeps without cease and demands that Xilie be held accountable;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Xilie's mother, consumed with love for her younger son, weeps without end and calls on Xilie to answer for his deeds;

sentences.zh: 又希烈妻祖母郭及妻妹封並逮捕京師。

translations.literal: Moreover Xilie's wife, his grandmother Guo, and his wife's younger sister Feng have all been arrested and brought to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Xilie's wife, his grandmother Lady Guo, and his wife's younger sister Lady Feng have all been seized and brought to the capital.

sentences.zh: 此三人留之無益，請寘境上以贖真卿，先降詔書，分明諭告。

translations.literal: Keeping these three persons serves no purpose; I beg that they be placed on the border to ransom Zhenqing, and that an edict be issued first, clearly instructing and proclaiming this.
translations.idiomatic: Detaining these three women serves no purpose; I ask that they be sent to the frontier to exchange for Zhenqing, after an edict has first been issued making the terms plain.

sentences.zh: 且希烈知真卿人望，不敢加害，既無嫌隙，但因循未遣耳。

translations.literal: Moreover Xilie knows Zhenqing's standing among men and dares not harm him; since there is no rancor between them, he has merely delayed in not sending him back.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Xilie knows Zhenqing's standing among men and will not dare harm him; with no real grievance between them, he has simply been slow to send him back.

sentences.zh: 若歸其親愛，賊亦何吝還一使哉？

translations.literal: If his loved ones are returned, what would the rebel begrudge in returning one envoy?
translations.idiomatic: If his kin are restored to him, what would the rebel begrudge in returning a single envoy?

sentences.zh: 臣又聞真卿所遣兄子峴及家僮從官奉表來者五輩，皆留中，其子頵等拳拳實希一見，望許休澣，告以安否。

translations.literal: I further hear that the five parties sent by Zhenqing—his elder brother's son Xian, household servants, and attendants bearing memorials—all have been kept within the palace; his son Yun and others earnestly long for a single meeting; I hope they may be granted leave on rest days to be told whether he is safe.
translations.idiomatic: I also hear that the five parties Zhenqing sent—his nephew Xian, servants, and attendants bearing memorials—have all been held in the palace; his son Yun and the others earnestly hope for even one meeting; I ask that they be granted leave on rest days to learn whether he is safe.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，盧杞持之，不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; Lu Qi withheld it and no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, but Lu Qi held it back and no response was issued.

sentences.zh: 朱泚反，詭姓名伏匿城中，著《史遁先生傳》。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled, [Jian] used a false name and hid within the city, composing the Biography of Master Shitun.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled, Jian assumed a false name and hid in the city, writing the Biography of Master Shitun.

sentences.zh: 京師平，擢左拾遺。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified, he was promoted to Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was restored, he was promoted to Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 詔復用杞為刺史，薦與陳京、趙需等論杞奸惡傾覆不當用，入對挺確，德宗納之。

translations.literal: An edict restored Qi to office as prefect; Jian, together with Chen Jing, Zhao Xu, and others, argued that Qi's treachery and wickedness made his restoration improper; on entering audience he spoke forthrightly and firmly, and Dezong accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict would have restored Qi as prefect; Jian joined Chen Jing, Zhao Xu, and others in arguing that Qi's treachery made him unfit for office; when he faced the throne he spoke bluntly and firmly, and Dezong accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，帝親郊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan, the emperor personally performed the suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenyuan the emperor performed the suburban sacrifice in person.

sentences.zh: 時更兵亂，禮物殘替，用薦為太常博士，參綴典儀，略如舊章。

translations.literal: At the time, after repeated military turmoil, ritual objects were damaged and missing; Jian was employed as erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to assist in arranging the ceremonial protocols, roughly according to the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The realm had just endured repeated warfare, and ritual implements were damaged or lost; Jian was made erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to help restore the ceremonies, roughly along the old regulations.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書關播持節送鹹安公主於回紇，以薦為判官。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Guan Bo, bearing the imperial staff, escorted Princess Xian'an to the Uyghurs; Jian served as his aide.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Guan Bo, bearing the imperial commission, escorted Princess Xian'an to the Uyghurs, with Jian as his aide.

sentences.zh: 還，遷工部員外郎。

translations.literal: On his return he was transferred to vice director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was promoted to vice director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢諫議大夫，復為史館修撰。

translations.literal: After some time he was promoted to Grand Master of Remonstrance and again served as compiler in the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was raised to Grand Master of Remonstrance and again appointed compiler in the Historiography Office.

sentences.zh: 方裴延齡用事，中傷俊良，建白無不當帝意。

translations.literal: Just then Pei Yanling was in power, slandering worthy men; every proposal he made suited the emperor's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Pei Yanling held sway, slandering worthy officials, and every proposal he made pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 薦將疏其惡，延齡知之，因言於帝曰：「諫議論朝政得失，史官書人君善惡，二者不可兼。

translations.literal: Jian was about to memorialize his wickedness; Yanling learned of it and therefore said to the emperor: "A remonstrator discusses the gains and losses of court affairs, while a historian records the ruler's good and evil— the two offices cannot be held together."
translations.idiomatic: Jian was preparing a memorial exposing his crimes; Yanling learned of it and told the emperor, "A remonstrator debates the rights and wrongs of court policy, while a historian records the ruler's virtues and faults—the two roles cannot be combined."

sentences.zh: 」薦改秘書少監。

translations.literal: " Jian was transferred to vice director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: " Jian was reassigned as vice director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 延齡必欲以罪斥廢之。

translations.literal: Yanling was determined to find fault and have him dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling was determined to find some charge and have him removed.

sentences.zh: 會遣使冊回鶻毗伽懷信可汗，使薦至回鶻。

translations.literal: It happened that envoys were dispatched to invest the Uyghur qaghan Bilge Huai Xin; Jian was sent to the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time envoys were sent to invest the Uyghur qaghan Bilge Huai Xin, and Jian was sent to the Uyghur court.

sentences.zh: 還為監。

translations.literal: On his return he became director [of the Palace Library].
translations.idiomatic: On his return he became director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃贊普死，擢薦工部侍郎，為吊祭使。

translations.literal: When the Tibetan tsenpo died, Jian was promoted to vice minister of works and made envoy of condolence and sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tibetan emperor died, Jian was promoted to vice minister of works and appointed envoy of condolence.

sentences.zh: 薦占對詳辯，三使絕域，始兼侍御史、中丞，後大夫。

translations.literal: Jian's divinations and replies were detailed and eloquent; on three missions to distant regions he first concurrently held the posts of attendant censor and vice censor-in-chief, then grand censor.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's divinations and replies were thorough and eloquent; on three missions beyond the frontier he first held concurrent posts as attendant censor and vice censor-in-chief, then as grand censor.

sentences.zh: 次赤嶺，被病卒，年六十一，吐蕃傳其柩以歸。

translations.literal: At Chiling he fell ill and died, aged sixty-one; the Tibetans conveyed his coffin back [to Tang territory].
translations.idiomatic: At Chiling he fell ill and died at sixty-one; the Tibetans escorted his coffin home.

sentences.zh: 順宗立，問至，贈禮部尚書，謚曰憲。

translations.literal: When Shunzong ascended, word of his death arrived; he was posthumously given the title Minister of Rites, with the posthumous name Xian.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong took the throne, news of his death arrived; he was posthumously made Minister of Rites, with the posthumous name Xian.

sentences.zh: 薦自拾遺至侍郎，凡二十年，常兼史館修撰。

translations.literal: From Reminder to vice minister, Jian served twenty years in all, usually also holding the concurrent post of compiler in the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: From his post as Reminder to vice minister, Jian served twenty years in all, usually also compiling at the Historiography Office.

sentences.zh: 初，貞元時，京師旱，帝避正殿，減膳，薦白限日以應古制。

translations.literal: Earlier, during Zhenyuan, when the capital suffered drought, the emperor avoided the main hall and reduced his meals; Jian memorialized that a time limit should be set in accord with ancient regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier in Zhenyuan, when drought struck the capital, the emperor left the main hall and cut his meals; Jian memorialized that a fixed term should be set in keeping with ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 及定昭德皇后廟樂，遷獻、懿二祖，定太儀位號、大臣祔廟鼓吹法，莫不參裁，諸儒謂博而詳。

translations.literal: When the temple music for Empress Zhaode was fixed, when the two ancestors Xian and Yi were moved, when the titles and ranks of the grand consorts were set, and when the regulations for enshrining chief ministers and for funeral processional music were determined—he took part in deliberating on all of these; the Confucian scholars said his knowledge was broad and detailed.
translations.idiomatic: Whether fixing the temple music for Empress Zhaode, moving the two ancestors Xian and Yi, setting titles for the grand consorts, or determining rules for enshrining chief ministers and funeral processional music, he took part in every deliberation; the scholars called his learning broad and thorough.

sentences.zh: 所著書百餘篇。

translations.literal: His written works numbered more than a hundred pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote more than a hundred works.

sentences.zh: 子又新，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Youxin has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Youxin has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 孫讀，字聖用，幼穎解。

translations.literal: His grandson Du, style name Shengyong, was clever and quick to understand from youth.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Du, styled Shengyong, was precociously quick-witted as a boy.

sentences.zh: 大中時第進士，鄭薰辟署宣州幕府。

translations.literal: During the Dazhong era he passed the jinshi examination; Zheng Xun recruited him to staff the Xuanzhou headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dazhong period he took the jinshi degree; Zheng Xun brought him into the Xuanzhou headquarters staff.

sentences.zh: 累遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 中和初為吏部，選牒精允。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhonghe he headed the Ministry of Personnel; his selection registers were precise and fair.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhonghe he headed the Ministry of Personnel, and his appointment registers were meticulous and fair.

sentences.zh: 調官丐留二年，詔可，榜其事曹門。

translations.literal: When his transfer came he begged to remain two years longer; an edict approved this, and his case was posted at the ministry gate.
translations.idiomatic: When his transfer order came he asked to stay two years longer; the court approved, and the matter was posted at the ministry gate.

sentences.zh: 後兼弘文館學士，判院事，卒。

translations.literal: Later he concurrently served as academician of the Hongwen Hall and directed its affairs, then died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he also served as academician of the Hongwen Hall and directed its affairs until his death.

sentences.zh: 趙涓，冀州人。

translations.literal: Zhao Juan was a native of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Juan came from Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 幼有文，天寶時第進士，補郾城尉，稍歷臺省。

translations.literal: In youth he had literary talent; during Tianbao he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed magistrate of Yancheng, and gradually served in the central ministries.
translations.idiomatic: He showed literary talent early; in the Tianbao era he took the jinshi degree, served as magistrate of Yancheng, and gradually rose through the central ministries.

sentences.zh: 河南王縉引署副元帥府判官。

translations.literal: Wang Jin, Prince of Henan, recruited him as aide in the deputy commander-in-chief's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin, Prince of Henan, brought him on as aide at the deputy commander-in-chief's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 德宗初，為衢州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dezong's reign he was prefect of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dezong's reign he served as prefect of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 始，永泰時，禁中火，近東宮，代宗疑之。

translations.literal: Earlier, during Yongtai, a fire broke out in the Forbidden City near the Eastern Palace, and Daizong was suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in Yongtai, a fire broke out in the palace precinct near the Eastern Palace, and Daizong grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 涓以監察御史為巡使，驗治明諦，跡火所來，乃宦人直舍。

translations.literal: Juan, as supervising censor serving as inspection envoy, investigated clearly and precisely; tracing whence the fire came, it proved to be the eunuchs' duty quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Juan, serving as supervising censor and inspection envoy, investigated with precision and traced the fire to the eunuchs' duty quarters.

sentences.zh: 帝在東宮頗德之。

translations.literal: The emperor, then in the Eastern Palace, was much indebted to him.
translations.idiomatic: The future emperor, then heir apparent, felt much indebted to him.

sentences.zh: 及治衢，不為觀察使韓滉所容，奏免官。

translations.literal: When he governed Quzhou he was not tolerated by the circuit commissioner Han Huang, who memorialized to have him dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: While governing Quzhou he fell out with the circuit commissioner Han Huang, who memorialized to have him removed from office.

sentences.zh: 帝見其名，問宰相曰：「是豈永泰時御史乎？

translations.literal: The emperor saw his name and asked the chief ministers: "Is this not the censor from Yongtai?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw his name and asked the chief ministers, "Is this not the censor from Yongtai?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「然。

translations.literal: " They answered: "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: " They answered, "It is."

sentences.zh: 」詔拜尚書左丞。

translations.literal: " An edict appointed him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict appointed him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 既至，勞之曰：「卿正直，朕所自知，乃以罪聞，不信也。

translations.literal: When he arrived, [the emperor] comforted him, saying: "You are upright—I know this myself; that you were reported for a crime, I do not believe."
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, the emperor comforted him, saying, "I know you are upright; I do not believe you committed any crime."

sentences.zh: 」命典吏部選。

translations.literal: " He ordered him to oversee selections in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: " He put him in charge of appointments at the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 從狩梁。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor on the hunt at Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor when the court withdrew to Liang.

sentences.zh: 興元元年卒，贈戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Xingyuan and was posthumously given the title Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Xingyuan and was posthumously made Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 子博宣，亦擢進士第。

translations.literal: His son Boxuan also passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His son Boxuan also took the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 藻翰豪邁，沈於酒，傲忽少檢。

translations.literal: His literary compositions were bold and expansive; he was sunk in wine, arrogant and neglectful, with little restraint.
translations.idiomatic: His writing was bold and expansive, but he was sunk in drink, arrogant and careless, with little sense of propriety.

sentences.zh: 陳許曲環辟署於府，久不能堪，乃誣「受吳少誠金為反間，數言休咎惑眾」。

translations.literal: Qu Huan of Chenxu recruited him to staff his headquarters; unable to endure him long, he falsely charged that "he received gold from Wu Shaochéng to serve as a spy, and repeatedly spoke of fortune and misfortune to delude the masses."
translations.idiomatic: Qu Huan of Chenxu brought him onto his staff, but after long could not tolerate him and falsely charged that "he took gold from Wu Shaochéng to act as a spy and repeatedly spoke omens to mislead the people."

sentences.zh: 有詔杖四十，流康州，時人冤之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered forty blows of the staff and exile to Kangzhou; people of the time considered it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered forty strokes of the rod and exile to Kangzhou; contemporaries regarded it as a grave injustice.

sentences.zh: 李紓，字仲舒。

translations.literal: Li Shu, style name Zhongshu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shu, whose style was Zhongshu.

sentences.zh: 始仕為校書郎，大歷初，李季卿薦為左補闕，遷累中書舍人。

translations.literal: He first served as collator; at the beginning of Dali, Li Jiqing recommended him as Left Supplementation Censor, and he was promoted through successive posts to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He began as collator; early in Dali Li Jiqing recommended him as Left Supplementation Censor, and he rose through successive posts to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 德宗居奉天，繇禮部侍郎選為同州刺史。

translations.literal: When Dezong was at Fengtian, he was transferred from vice minister of rites to be prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: While Dezong was at Fengtian, Shu was moved from vice minister of rites to prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝次梁，紓委城趨行在，擢兵部侍郎、高邑伯。

translations.literal: When the emperor halted at Liang, Shu left his prefecture and hastened to the mobile court; he was promoted to vice minister of war and enfeoffed as Baron of Gaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor stopped at Liang, Shu left his post and hurried to the mobile court; he was promoted to vice minister of war and enfeoffed as Baron of Gaoyi.

sentences.zh: 建言享武成王廟不宜與文宣王等，制從之。

translations.literal: He proposed that sacrifices at the temple of the Martial Completion King should not be ranked equal to those of the Civil Propagation King; an edict followed his view.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that sacrifices at the temple of the Martial Completion King should not be ranked equal to those of Confucius; the court adopted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 紓性樂易，喜接後進。

translations.literal: Shu's nature was cheerful and easygoing; he delighted in receiving younger scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was cheerful and easygoing and delighted in welcoming younger scholars.

sentences.zh: 其自奉養頗華裕，不為齪齪崖檢。

translations.literal: His own maintenance of himself was quite lavish and comfortable; he was not petty or rigid in restraint.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in considerable comfort and was not petty or rigid about propriety.

sentences.zh: 官雖貴，則遊縱自如。

translations.literal: Though his office was exalted, he roamed and indulged himself freely.
translations.idiomatic: Even when his rank was high, he roamed and enjoyed himself freely.

sentences.zh: 奉詔為《興元紀功述》及它郊廟樂章，論撰甚多。

translations.literal: By imperial command he composed the Account of Achievements at Xingyuan and other suburban and temple ritual hymns; his treatises and writings were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial command he wrote the Account of Achievements at Xingyuan and other suburban and temple hymns; his essays and compositions were very numerous.

sentences.zh: 進吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 年六十二卒，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-two and was posthumously given the title Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-two and was posthumously made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 鄭雲達，系本滎陽。

translations.literal: Zheng Yunda's clan origin was Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yunda's family came from Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 父戶，為郾城尉，州刺史移職，民之暴謷者遮道留，戶誅殺六七人。

translations.literal: His father Hu served as magistrate of Yancheng; when the prefect was transferred, violent and clamorous commoners blocked the road to detain him, and Hu killed six or seven men.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hu was magistrate of Yancheng; when the prefect was transferred, violent townspeople blocked the road to keep him, and Hu killed six or seven of them.

sentences.zh: 采訪使奇之，言狀，擢北海尉。

translations.literal: The investigation commissioner considered this remarkable, reported the circumstances, and he was promoted to magistrate of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: The investigation commissioner was impressed, reported what had happened, and Hu was promoted to magistrate of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，縣民孫俊驅市人以應，戶率眾擊殺之。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, the county commoner Sun Jun drove market people to respond; Hu led the crowd to attack and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, a county man named Sun Jun drove townspeople to join the rebels; Hu led the people in attacking and killing him.

sentences.zh: 改登州司馬。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military aide of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military aide of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 李光弼表為武寧府判官，遷沂州刺史，諭降賊李浩五千人。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi memorialized him as aide in the Wuning headquarters; he was transferred to prefect of Yizhou and persuaded five thousand rebels under Li Hao to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi recommended him as aide at the Wuning headquarters; he was made prefect of Yizhou and persuaded five thousand rebels under Li Hao to submit.

sentences.zh: 終滁州刺史。

translations.literal: He ended his career as prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 雲達為人誕譎敢言，已登進士第，去客燕朔，朱泚善之，表為掌書記，妻以滔女。

translations.literal: Yunda was by nature boastful and crafty, bold in speech; having passed the jinshi examination, he left to sojourn in Yan and Shuobei; Zhu Ci favored him, memorialized him as chief secretary, and gave him Zhu Tao's daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Yunda was boastful and crafty and spoke boldly; after taking the jinshi degree he went to serve as a guest in Yan and Shuobei; Zhu Ci favored him, made him chief secretary, and married him to Zhu Tao's daughter.

sentences.zh: 泚將朝，使雲達先入奏，同府蔡廷玉譖於泚，奏貶為平州參軍。

translations.literal: When Ci was about to attend court, he sent Yunda ahead to present a memorial; Cai Tingyu of the same headquarters slandered him to Ci, and a memorial demoted him to military aide of Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Ci was about to go to court, he sent Yunda ahead to present a memorial; Cai Tingyu of the same staff slandered him to Ci, and Yunda was demoted to military aide of Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 滔代泚將，復辟雲達為判官。

translations.literal: Tao replaced Ci as commander and again recruited Yunda as aide.
translations.idiomatic: Tao took Ci's place as commander and again brought Yunda on as aide.

sentences.zh: 廷玉與要藉官朱體微它日與泚從容言：「滔非長者，不可付以兵。

translations.literal: Tingyu and the key-attendance official Zhu Tiwei one day spoke at ease with Ci, saying: "Tao is not a man of mature character and cannot be entrusted with troops."
translations.idiomatic: One day Tingyu and the key-attendance official Zhu Tiwei spoke casually with Ci, saying, "Tao is not a man of mature character and should not be given command of troops."

sentences.zh: 」雲達數漏其語以怒滔，故滔論廷玉等，皆得罪死。

translations.literal: " Yunda repeatedly leaked their words to enrage Tao; therefore Tao prosecuted Tingyu and the others, and all were condemned to death.
translations.idiomatic: " Yunda repeatedly leaked their words to anger Tao, so Tao prosecuted Tingyu and the others, and all were put to death.

sentences.zh: 滔助田悅，雲達諫，不從，遂棄室自歸。

translations.literal: Tao aided Tian Yue; Yunda remonstrated but was not heeded, so he abandoned his household and returned on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Tao aided Tian Yue; Yunda remonstrated but was ignored, so he left his family and returned to Tang territory on his own.

sentences.zh: 德宗悅，擢諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Dezong was pleased and promoted him to Grand Master of Remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong was pleased and promoted him to Grand Master of Remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 帝在梁，雲達依李晟，晟表以禮部侍郎為軍司馬，時時咨逮戎略。

translations.literal: When the emperor was at Liang, Yunda attached himself to Li Sheng; Sheng memorialized that he serve as army marshal with the title vice minister of rites, and frequently consulted him on military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was at Liang, Yunda joined Li Sheng, who recommended him as army marshal with the title vice minister of rites and often consulted him on military strategy.

sentences.zh: 元和初，為京兆尹，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, then died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanhe he became metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and died in office.

sentences.zh: 弟方達，悖悍，結徒剽劫，父欲殺之，不克。

translations.literal: His younger brother Fangda was perverse and fierce, gathered followers to plunder and rob; their father wished to kill him but could not.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Fangda was violent and fierce and gathered a band to rob and plunder; their father wanted to kill him but could not.

sentences.zh: 雲達自劾「不能教，恐赤臣家」。

translations.literal: Yunda impeached himself, saying "I could not teach him and fear I will bring shame upon the loyal household."
translations.idiomatic: Yunda impeached himself, saying, "I failed to teach him and fear I will bring disgrace on our loyal family."

sentences.zh: 詔錮死黔州。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him imprisoned until death in Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him imprisoned until death in Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 徐岱，字處仁，蘇州嘉興人，世農家子。

translations.literal: Xu Dai, style name Churen, was a native of Jiaxing in Suzhou, from a farming family for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Dai, styled Churen, came from Jiaxing in Suzhou; his family had been farmers for generations.

sentences.zh: 於學無所不通，辯論明銳，座人常屈。

translations.literal: In learning there was nothing he did not master; his debate was sharp and clear, and those seated with him were often put to rout.
translations.idiomatic: There was no branch of learning he had not mastered; in debate he was sharp and clear, and those who sat with him were often bested.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，劉晏表為校書郎。

translations.literal: During Dali, Liu Yan memorialized him as collator.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali period Liu Yan recommended him as collator.

sentences.zh: 觀察使李棲筠欽其賢，署所居為「復禮鄉」。

translations.literal: The commissioner Li Qiyun admired his worth and designated his residence as "Restoring Rites Township."
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Li Qiyun admired his virtue and named his home district "Restoring Rites Township."

sentences.zh: 名達於朝，擢偃師尉。

translations.literal: His name reached the court, and he was promoted to magistrate of Yanshi.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation reached court, and he was promoted to magistrate of Yanshi.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使蔣鎮薦為太常博士，專掌禮事。

translations.literal: The ritual commissioner Jiang Zhen recommended him as erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, exclusively in charge of ritual affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual Commissioner Jiang Zhen recommended him as erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, put in sole charge of ritual matters.

sentences.zh: 從德宗出奉天，以膳部員外郎兼博士。

translations.literal: He followed Dezong when the emperor went out to Fengtian, serving as vice director of the Bureau of Provisions while also holding the post of erudite.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Dezong when the court withdrew to Fengtian, serving as vice director of the Bureau of Provisions while also holding the post of erudite.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，為太子、諸王侍讀，遷給事中、史館修撰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan he was reader to the crown prince and the princes, then was transferred to supervising secretary and compiler in the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyuan he served as reader to the crown prince and the princes, then was promoted to supervising secretary and compiler at the Historiography Office.

sentences.zh: 帝以誕日歲歲詔佛老者大論麟德殿，並召岱及趙需、許孟容、韋渠牟講說。

translations.literal: On his birthday each year the emperor ordered great debates between Buddhists and Daoists in the Linde Hall, and summoned Dai together with Zhao Xu, Xu Mengrong, and Wei Qiumou to lecture.
translations.idiomatic: Each year on his birthday the emperor ordered great debates between Buddhists and Daoists in the Linde Hall and summoned Dai along with Zhao Xu, Xu Mengrong, and Wei Qiumou to lecture.

sentences.zh: 始三家若矛楯然，卒而同歸於善。

translations.literal: At first the three schools were like spear and shield, but in the end all returned to what was good.
translations.idiomatic: At first the three schools clashed like spear against shield, but in the end all converged on what was good.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，賚予有差。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed rewards in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed rewards in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 兩宮恩遇無比。

translations.literal: The favor shown him by the two palaces was without parallel.
translations.idiomatic: The favor shown him by the emperor and empress was unmatched.

sentences.zh: 性篤慎，至宮殿中語未嘗近之，不談人短，宗族孤孺者皆為婚嫁。

translations.literal: His nature was sincere and cautious; even in the palace his speech never drew near impropriety; he did not discuss others' faults; for orphaned and young kin in the clan he arranged marriages.
translations.idiomatic: He was sincere and cautious; even in the palace he never spoke improperly, never discussed others' faults, and arranged marriages for orphaned kin in the clan.

sentences.zh: 然吝嗇，自持家管鑰，世所譏雲。

translations.literal: Yet he was stingy, keeping the household keys himself—a thing the age mocked.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was stingy and kept the household keys himself, which people of the day mocked.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given the title Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 王仲舒，字弘中，并州祁人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongshu, style name Hongzhong, was a native of Qi in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongshu, styled Hongzhong, came from Qi in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 少客江南，與梁肅、楊憑遊，有文稱。

translations.literal: In youth he sojourned in the south, associated with Liang Su and Yang Ping, and had a reputation for literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he lived in the south, associated with Liang Su and Yang Ping, and won a reputation for literary talent.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，賢良方正高第，拜左拾遺。

translations.literal: During Zhenyuan he received top marks in the Worthy and Upright recruitment and was appointed Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenyuan he earned top marks in the Worthy and Upright examination and was appointed Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 德宗欲相裴延齡，與陽城交章言不可。

translations.literal: When Dezong wished to make Pei Yanling chief minister, he and Yang Cheng submitted successive memorials saying this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong wished to make Pei Yanling chief minister, he and Yang Cheng submitted successive memorials arguing that it must not be done.

sentences.zh: 後入閣，帝顧宰相指曰：「是豈王仲舒邪？

translations.literal: Later when he entered the privy council, the emperor looked at the chief ministers and pointed, saying: "Is that not Wang Zhongshu?"
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he entered the privy council, the emperor looked at the chief ministers and pointed, saying, "Is that not Wang Zhongshu?"

sentences.zh: 」俄改右補闕，遷禮部考功員外郎。

translations.literal: " Shortly after he was changed to Right Supplementation Censor and transferred to vice director of evaluations in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: " Shortly after he was made Right Supplementation Censor and promoted to vice director of evaluations in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 奏議詳雅，省中伏其能。

translations.literal: His memorials and proposals were detailed and elegant; within the ministry all acknowledged his ability.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials were thorough and elegant, and everyone in the ministry respected his ability.

sentences.zh: 坐累為連州司戶參軍，再徙荊南節度參謀。

translations.literal: Through implication in a case he became revenue aide of Lianzhou, then was transferred again as staff officer to the Jingnan command.
translations.idiomatic: Implicated in a case, he was made revenue aide of Lianzhou, then transferred as staff officer to the Jingnan command.

sentences.zh: 元和初，召為吏部員外郎，未幾，知制誥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was summoned as vice director of the Ministry of Personnel; before long he was put in charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanhe he was summoned as vice director of the Ministry of Personnel and soon put in charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 楊憑得罪斥去，無敢過其家，仲舒屢存之。

translations.literal: When Yang Ping was condemned and driven away, no one dared visit his home; Zhongshu repeatedly went to see him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Ping was condemned and driven from office, no one dared visit his home, but Zhongshu went to see him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 將直憑冤，貶峽州刺史，母喪解。

translations.literal: About to speak out on Ping's injustice, he was demoted to prefect of Xiazhou; he resigned on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to speak out on Ping's injustice, he was demoted to prefect of Xiazhou; he resigned when his mother died.

sentences.zh: 服除，為婺州刺史。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was made prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was made prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 州疫旱，人徙死幾空；

translations.literal: The prefecture suffered plague and drought; people fled and died until it was nearly empty;
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture was struck by plague and drought; people fled and died until the region was nearly empty;

sentences.zh: 居五年，裏閭增完，就加金紫服。

translations.literal: after five years in office the villages and lanes were increasingly restored, and he was thereupon given the gold-and-purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: after five years the villages were largely restored, and he was given the gold-and-purple robe.

sentences.zh: 徙蘇州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 堤松江為路，變屋瓦，絕火災，賦調嘗與民為期，不擾自辦。

translations.literal: He diked the Song River to make a road, changed roof tiles [to tile instead of thatch], and ended fires; for tax levies he once set deadlines with the people, and without disturbance they completed them on their own.
translations.idiomatic: He diked the Song River to make a road, required tile roofs instead of thatch to end fires, and when he set tax deadlines with the people they met them without being pressed.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，每言仲舒之文可思，最宜為誥，有古風。

translations.literal: When Muzong ascended, he often said Zhongshu's writings were worth pondering, most suited for edicts of investiture, and had an antique style.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong took the throne, he often said Zhongshu's prose was worth pondering, best suited for edicts of investiture, and had an antique style.

sentences.zh: 召為中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 既至，視同列率新進少年，居不樂，曰：「豈可復治筆研於其間哉！

translations.literal: When he arrived, he saw his colleagues were mostly newly risen young men and was discontent, saying: "How could I again grind ink and wield the brush among them!"
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, he found his colleagues were mostly young newcomers and was unhappy, saying, "How can I grind ink and write among them again!"

sentences.zh: 吾久棄外，周知俗病利，得治之，不自愧。

translations.literal: I have long been cast out abroad and thoroughly know the people's ills and gains; if I can govern them, I will not feel ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: I have long served outside the capital and know the people's troubles and needs well; if I can govern them, I will not feel ashamed.

sentences.zh: 」宰相聞之，除江西觀察使。

translations.literal: " The chief ministers heard this and appointed him commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: " The chief ministers heard this and made him commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 初，江西榷酒利多佗州十八，民私釀，歲抵死不絕，谷數斛易鬥酒。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jiangxi's wine monopoly profits exceeded those of other prefectures by eighteenfold; the people brewed privately, and each year those condemned to death for it never ceased; several hu of grain could be exchanged for a dou of wine.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jiangxi's wine monopoly profits exceeded those of other circuits eighteenfold; people brewed illegally year after year, and several bushels of grain could buy a pint of wine.

sentences.zh: 仲舒罷酤錢九十萬。

translations.literal: Zhongshu abolished nine hundred thousand in wine-sale revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu abolished nine hundred thousand in wine monopoly revenue.

sentences.zh: 吏坐失官息錢五十萬，悉產不能償，仲舒焚簿書，脫械不問。

translations.literal: Officials were implicated for losing five hundred thousand in official interest money; their entire property could not repay it; Zhongshu burned the account books, removed their shackles, and did not pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were charged with losing five hundred thousand in official interest; their entire property could not cover the debt; Zhongshu burned the account books, removed their shackles, and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 水旱，民賦不入，嘆曰：「我當減燕樂他用可乎！

translations.literal: During flood and drought the people's taxes did not come in; he sighed and said: "Should I reduce banquet music and use the savings elsewhere?"
translations.idiomatic: During flood and drought the people could not pay taxes; he sighed and said, "Should I cut back on banquet music and use the savings elsewhere?"

sentences.zh: 」為出錢二千萬代之。

translations.literal: " He paid out twenty million cash to cover it for them.
translations.idiomatic: " He paid out twenty million cash to cover the shortfall for them.

sentences.zh: 有為佛老法、興浮屠祠屋者，皆驅出境。

translations.literal: Those who practiced Buddhist or Daoist ways and built Buddhist shrine halls were all driven beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who preached Buddhist or Daoist teachings or built Buddhist shrines was driven out of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 卒於官，年六十二，贈左散騎常侍，謚曰成。

translations.literal: He died in office at sixty-two; he was posthumously given the title Left Regular Attendant and the posthumous name Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at sixty-two and was posthumously made Left Regular Attendant, with the posthumous name Cheng.

sentences.zh: 仲舒尚義概，所居急民廢置，自為科條，初若煩密，久皆稱其便。

translations.literal: Zhongshu valued righteousness and magnanimity; wherever he served he urgently addressed the people's neglected needs, drawing up regulations himself; at first they seemed troublesome and detailed, but in time all praised their convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu valued righteousness and public spirit; wherever he served he urgently addressed neglected public needs and drew up regulations himself; at first they seemed burdensome, but in time everyone praised their convenience.

sentences.zh: 馮伉，魏州元城人，徙貫京兆。

translations.literal: Feng Kang was a native of Yuancheng in Weizhou and later registered his domicile in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Kang came from Yuancheng in Weizhou and later registered his domicile in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 第五經、宏辭，調長安尉。

translations.literal: He passed the fifth classics examination and the grand eloquence examination and was transferred as magistrate of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the fifth classics and grand eloquence examinations and was appointed magistrate of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 三遷膳部員外郎，為睦王等侍讀。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became vice director of the Bureau of Provisions and reader to the Prince of Mu and others.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became vice director of the Bureau of Provisions and reader to the Prince of Mu and others.

sentences.zh: 李抱真卒，伉持節臨吊，歸之帛，不受，又致京師，伉上表固拒。

translations.literal: When Li Baozhen died, Kang went bearing the imperial staff to offer condolences; on his return they gave him silk, which he did not accept; when it was again sent to the capital, Kang submitted a memorial firmly refusing it.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Baozhen died, Kang went with the imperial commission to offer condolences; on his return they gave him silk, which he refused; when it was sent again to the capital, Kang submitted a memorial firmly refusing it.

sentences.zh: 於是醴泉令缺，宰相高選，德宗曰：「前使澤潞不受幣者，其人清，可用也。

translations.literal: Then the magistracy of Liquan was vacant and the chief ministers made a high selection; Dezong said: "The one who earlier went to Ze and Lu and did not accept gifts—that man is pure and can be used."
translations.idiomatic: When the magistracy of Liquan fell vacant and the chief ministers made a careful selection, Dezong said, "The envoy who went to Ze and Lu and refused gifts—that man is upright and can be used."

sentences.zh: 」遂以授伉。

translations.literal: " Accordingly the post was given to Kang.
translations.idiomatic: " The post was accordingly given to Kang.

sentences.zh: 縣多嚚猾，數犯法，伉為著《諭蒙書》十四篇，大抵勸之務農、進學而教以忠孝。

translations.literal: The county had many violent and cunning men who repeatedly broke the law; Kang composed fourteen chapters of the Book for Instructing the Young, mostly urging them to devote themselves to farming and advance in learning while teaching loyalty and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: The county had many violent and cunning men who repeatedly broke the law; Kang wrote fourteen chapters of the Book for Instructing the Young, urging people to farm, study, and practice loyalty and filial piety.

sentences.zh: 鄉鄉授之，使轉相教督。

translations.literal: He gave it out township by township, having them teach and supervise one another in turn.
translations.idiomatic: He distributed it township by township and had people teach and supervise one another.

sentences.zh: 居七年，韋渠牟薦為給事中、皇太子諸王侍讀。

translations.literal: After seven years in office, Wei Qiumou recommended him as supervising secretary and reader to the crown prince and the princes.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years Wei Qiumou recommended him as supervising secretary and reader to the crown prince and the princes.

sentences.zh: 對殿中，賜金紫服。

translations.literal: He was received in audience in the hall and granted the gold-and-purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: He was received in audience in the hall and granted the gold-and-purple robe.

sentences.zh: 進兵部侍郎，出為同州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of war and went out as prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of war and sent out as prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 以散騎常侍召，領國子祭酒者再。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Regular Attendant and twice headed the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Regular Attendant and twice served as director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十六，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-six and was posthumously given the title Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-six and was posthumously made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 庾敬休，字順之，鄧州新野人。

translations.literal: Yu Jingxiu, style name Shunzhi, was a native of Xinye in Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jingxiu, styled Shunzhi, came from Xinye in Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖光烈，與弟光先不受安祿山偽官，遁去。

translations.literal: His grandfather Guanglie and his younger brother Guangxian did not accept false offices from An Lushan and fled away.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Guanglie and his younger brother Guangxian refused false offices under An Lushan and fled.

sentences.zh: 光烈終大理少卿，光先吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Guanglie ended as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review; Guangxian as vice minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Guanglie ended as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review; Guangxian as vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 父何，當朱泚反，又與弟倬逃山谷，不臣賊。

translations.literal: His father He, when Zhu Ci rebelled, again fled with his younger brother Zhuo into the mountains and valleys and did not submit to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: His father He, when Zhu Ci rebelled, again fled with his younger brother Zhuo into the mountains and would not submit to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 官兵部郎中。

translations.literal: He ended as director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 敬休擢進士第，又中宏辭，辟宣州幕府。

translations.literal: Jingxiu passed the jinshi examination and also passed the grand eloquence examination; he was recruited to the Xuanzhou headquarters staff.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxiu took the jinshi degree and also passed the grand eloquence examination, then joined the Xuanzhou headquarters staff.

sentences.zh: 入拜右補闕、起居舍人，建言：「天子視朝，宰相群臣以次對，言可傳後者，承旨宰相示左右起居，則載錄，季送史官，如故事。

translations.literal: He entered court as Right Supplementation Censor and Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and proposed: "When the Son of Heaven holds court, the chief ministers and officials respond in turn; statements fit to be passed down should be shown by the edict-drafting chief minister to the left and right attendants of the heir apparent, who shall record them and at season's end send them to the historiographers, as precedent provides."
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Right Supplementation Censor and Attendant of the Heir Apparent and proposed that when the emperor held court, statements worth preserving should be shown by the edict-drafting chief minister to the attendants of the heir apparent for recording and sent quarterly to the historiographers, as precedent provided.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: " An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 既而執政以幾密有不可露，罷之。

translations.literal: Before long the chief ministers, on the grounds that some matters were secret and could not be disclosed, abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the chief ministers abolished the practice on the grounds that some matters were too secret to disclose.

sentences.zh: 召為翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 文宗將立魯王為太子，慎選師傅，敬休以戶部侍郎兼魯王傅。

translations.literal: When Wenzong was about to establish the Prince of Lu as crown prince, he carefully selected tutors; Jingxiu served as vice minister of revenue while also tutor to the Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong was about to make the Prince of Lu crown prince, he carefully chose tutors; Jingxiu served as vice minister of revenue while also tutor to the Prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 初，劍南西川、山南道歲征茶，戶部自遣巡院主之，募賈人入錢京師。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jiannan West and the Shannan circuit levied tea tax each year; the Ministry of Revenue itself dispatched inspection offices to oversee it and recruited merchants to remit money to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jiannan West and the Shannan circuit levied an annual tea tax; the Ministry of Revenue sent inspection offices to oversee collection and recruited merchants to remit funds to the capital.

sentences.zh: 太和初，崔元略奏責本道主當歲以四萬緡上度支。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, Cui Yuanlue memorialized that the circuit itself should be responsible each year for remitting forty thousand strings to the Department of Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taihe Cui Yuanlue memorialized that each circuit should itself remit forty thousand strings annually to the Department of Treasury.

sentences.zh: 久之，逗留多不至。

translations.literal: After a long time, delays were frequent and remittances often did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Over time delays became frequent and remittances often failed to arrive.

sentences.zh: 敬休始請置院秭歸，收度支錢，乃無逋沒。

translations.literal: Jingxiu first proposed establishing an office at Zigui to collect the treasury funds, and thereafter there were no defaults.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxiu first proposed establishing a collection office at Zigui to gather treasury funds, and thereafter there were no shortfalls.

sentences.zh: 又言：「蜀道米價騰踴，百姓流亡，請以本道闕官職田賑貧民。

translations.literal: He also said: "On the Shu road grain prices are soaring, and the common people are fleeing; I beg that vacant official salary lands in this circuit be used to relieve the poor."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Grain prices on the Shu road are soaring and the people are fleeing; I ask that vacant official salary lands in this circuit be used to relieve the poor."

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: " An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 再為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He again served as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given the title Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 敬休夷淡，多容可，不飲酒食肉，不邇聲色。

translations.literal: Jingxiu was mild and plain, very accommodating, did not drink wine or eat meat, and did not draw near to music and women.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxiu was mild and plain, very accommodating, abstained from wine and meat, and kept away from music and women.

sentences.zh: 弟簡休，亦至工部侍郎。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jianxiu also reached the post of vice minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Jianxiu also rose to vice minister of works.
